newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland police patrol hit by blast.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland police patrol hit by blast.

text.p: A police patrol in Northern Ireland escaped injury in a bomb attack on Tuesday, police said.

The explosion occurred in the Shantallow area of the province's second city of Londonderry as a two-vehicle police patrol was passing, a police spokesman said. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack but security sources said it bore the hallmarks of the Irish Republican Army, fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland.
The police spokesman said it was not immediately clear if a bomb had exploded at the side of the road or whether it had been fired at the patrol.
The area was immediately cordoned off by security forces who were expected to start a detailed examination after dawn.
The blast occurred close to a crowded sports complex where swimming classes were in progress.

A pro-British local politician, Democratic Unionist Party councillor Gregory Campbell, said the attack demonstrated the "hypocrisy" of the IRA's political wing, Sinn Fein, which is pressing for a place at multiparty peace talks in Northern Ireland.

The incident came as police in Northern Ireland questioned two men over an Irish Republican Army rocket attack on the High Court in Belfast on Monday, which raised fears of retaliation by pro-British "Loyalist" guerrillas.
After that attack, security forces were on heightened alert for further violence.

Earlier on Tuesday, police carried out a controlled explosion on a suspect car in Belfast's Ormeau road area and also evacuated the Europa, the city's premier hotel, after a telephoned bomb warning. No device was found.

British Prime Minister John Major, architect of the slow-moving Northern Ireland peace process, said Monday's Belfast attack made it hard to believe that Sinn Fein could take part in the negotiations.
The party is excluded from the talks until the IRA calls a permanent halt to a campaign it launched in February last year when it ended a 17-month truce.
Police fear IRA violence may further strain a 26-month-old truce by the IRA's enemies -- Protestant Loyalists who want the province to stay British.

Spokesmen for political groups close to the Loyalists said that as far as they knew the ceasefire was still intact but weekend press reports quoted Loyalist activists as saying they would avenge IRA violence with attacks of their own.
